metricsExplanation.dataBody: We rebuild daily market values for every holding using the latest price data and any recorded corporate actions. Cash flows, trades and benchmark levels are normalised to UTC trading days. Metrics refresh whenever new prices are ingested.
metricsExplanation.disclaimer: These statistics are provided for information only and may differ from figures reported by your broker if their pricing or benchmark selection differs.
metricsExplanation.intro: These metrics summarise how the combined portfolio performs relative to its benchmark. Each value is derived from the same daily return series that powers the dashboard tiles.
metricsExplanation.loadError: We couldn’t load the latest metrics: {{message}}
metricsExplanation.missingContext: This page explains the metrics and jargon used across the app. It also shows live numbers when opened from a specific portfolio or group — open it from the Performance page (or a “Learn more” link elsewhere in the app) to see your own figures filled in below.
metricsExplanation.noContext: Open this page from a portfolio or group to see live numbers.

alpha.breakdownIntro: Each row shows how the cumulative portfolio and benchmark returns evolve on the same trading days. Their difference is the excess return (alpha).
alpha.calculation: We compute time-weighted cumulative returns for both the portfolio and the configured benchmark. Alpha is simply the portfolio return minus the benchmark return, expressed in percentage points.
alpha.detail: Cumulative portfolio return: {{portfolio}} · Benchmark return: {{benchmark}} · Alpha: {{alpha}}
alpha.headline: Alpha vs Benchmark
notes: Positive alpha means the portfolio outperformed the benchmark over the selected period.
If either return series is unavailable for the full span we fall back to the overlapping dates only.
alpha.summary: Alpha measures the portfolio's excess return after matching the benchmark over the same date range.
alpha.title: Alpha vs Benchmark

maxDrawdown.breakdownIntro: We rebuild the portfolio value curve, track each rolling peak, and compute the drawdown at every point. The minimum of this series is the max drawdown shown above.
maxDrawdown.calculation: We scan the time-weighted return curve, track each new peak, and record the largest subsequent drop before a new peak is reached. The deepest percentage loss becomes the max drawdown.
maxDrawdown.detail: Max drawdown: {{drawdown}} · Peak: {{peakValue}} on {{peakDate}} · Trough: {{troughValue}} on {{troughDate}}
maxDrawdown.headline: Worst peak-to-trough move
notes: Drawdown is calculated on portfolio returns only; the benchmark is not considered here.
A -100% drawdown would mean the portfolio value reached zero after a prior peak.
maxDrawdown.summary: Max drawdown identifies the worst peak-to-trough decline in portfolio value over the measurement window.
maxDrawdown.title: Max Drawdown

trackingError.breakdownIntro: Daily active returns (portfolio minus benchmark) are listed below. The standard deviation of this series, scaled by √252, produces the tracking error above.
trackingError.calculation: For each trading day we take the portfolio return minus the benchmark return, producing an active return series. Tracking error is the annualised standard deviation of those active returns (daily standard deviation multiplied by √252).
trackingError.detail: Annualised tracking error: {{trackingError}} · Daily active-return standard deviation: {{dailyStd}}
trackingError.headline: Tracking error and daily active returns
notes: Higher tracking error indicates looser alignment with the benchmark.
We require at least 30 overlapping daily returns to display this metric.
trackingError.summary: Tracking error captures the variability of active returns—how much the portfolio's daily returns diverge from the benchmark.
trackingError.title: Tracking Error

otherPerformance.title: More performance measures
otherPerformance.intro: These also appear on the Performance page but don't need live data to explain.

twr.title: Time-Weighted Return
twr.detail: Time-weighted return measures the portfolio's compounded growth rate over the selected period by linking together each sub-period's return. It removes the effect of the timing and size of deposits and withdrawals, so it reflects how the underlying investments performed rather than when money moved in or out.

xirr.title: XIRR
xirr.detail: XIRR is the annualised internal rate of return calculated from the portfolio's actual dated cash flows (deposits, withdrawals, and current value). Unlike time-weighted return, it is affected by the timing and size of those cash flows.

trading.title: Trading signal terms
trading.intro: Terms used on the Trading page's strategy thresholds and signal table.

rsi.title: RSI (Relative Strength Index)
rsi.detail: RSI is a momentum indicator, scored 0-100, derived from recent price changes. “RSI buy below” and “RSI sell above” are the thresholds a signal's RSI value must reach — at or below the buy threshold, at or above the sell threshold — to be considered a buy or sell candidate. “RSI lookback” is the number of days of price history used to calculate it.

movingAverage.title: Moving average (short / long)
movingAverage.detail: A moving average is the average closing price over a fixed number of days. Signals compare a shorter-window average against a longer-window one; the two windows are configured separately as “Short moving average” and “Long moving average”.

sharpe.title: Sharpe ratio
sharpe.detail: Here, the Sharpe ratio is the excess return over the configured risk-free rate per unit of daily volatility, annualised (× √252). “Minimum Sharpe ratio” is an optional filter threshold a signal's Sharpe ratio must meet, when that filter is enabled.

debtEquity.title: Debt/equity (D/E)
debtEquity.detail: Debt/equity divides a company's total debt by its shareholders' equity — a measure of financial leverage. “Maximum debt/equity” is an optional filter threshold, when enabled.

volatility.title: Volatility
volatility.detail: Here, volatility is the day-to-day (daily, not annualised) standard deviation of returns — how much the price has fluctuated from one day to the next. “Maximum volatility” is an optional filter threshold, when enabled.

checksSkipped.title: “Checks skipped”
checksSkipped.detail: This badge appears when an optional check that needs the allotmint-pro add-on could not run, because that add-on isn't installed. “compliance” means the trade was not checked against your compliance rules at all. “fundamental_screen” means the P/E and debt/equity filters (configured above) were not applied to this buy candidate.

screener.title: Screener ratios
screener.intro: The Screener page filters instruments by these financial ratios.

peg.title: PEG ratio
peg.detail: P/E ratio divided by the expected earnings growth rate.

pe.title: P/E ratio
pe.detail: Share price divided by earnings per share.

pb.title: P/B ratio
pb.detail: Share price divided by book value per share. Below 1 means the market values the company at less than its net assets on paper.

ps.title: P/S ratio
ps.detail: Market capitalisation divided by trailing twelve-month revenue. Useful where earnings are negative or volatile.

evEbitda.title: EV/EBITDA
evEbitda.detail: Enterprise value (market cap plus net debt) divided by EBITDA. Compares companies regardless of how they are financed.

revenueGrowth.title: Revenue growth
revenueGrowth.detail: Year-on-year revenue growth, as a fraction (0.1 = 10%).

earningsGrowth.title: Earnings growth
earningsGrowth.detail: Year-on-year earnings growth, as a fraction (0.1 = 10%).

ltDe.title: LT D/E ratio
ltDe.detail: Long-term debt divided by shareholders' equity.

interestCoverage.title: Interest coverage
interestCoverage.detail: Operating earnings (EBIT) divided by interest expense — how many times over a company could pay its interest from its earnings.

currentRatio.title: Current ratio
currentRatio.detail: Current assets divided by current liabilities.

quickRatio.title: Quick ratio
quickRatio.detail: Liquid assets, excluding inventory, divided by current liabilities.

fcf.title: FCF (Free cash flow)
fcf.detail: Cash generated from operations minus capital expenditure.

eps.title: EPS (Earnings per share)
eps.detail: Net income divided by the number of shares outstanding.

ebitdaMargin.title: EBITDA margin
ebitdaMargin.detail: EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) divided by revenue.

roa.title: ROA (Return on assets)
roa.detail: Net income divided by total assets.

roe.title: ROE (Return on equity)
roe.detail: Net income divided by shareholders' equity.

roi.title: ROI (Return on investment)
roi.detail: The gain from an investment divided by its cost.

dividendYield.title: Dividend yield
dividendYield.detail: Annual dividend per share divided by share price.

dividendPayoutRatio.title: Dividend payout ratio
dividendPayoutRatio.detail: Dividends paid divided by net income.

beta.title: Beta
beta.detail: A measure of how sensitive a stock's price is to overall market movements.

sharesOutstanding.title: Shares outstanding
sharesOutstanding.detail: The total number of a company's shares currently held by all shareholders.

floatShares.title: Float shares
floatShares.detail: Shares outstanding that are freely tradable, excluding closely held or restricted shares.

marketCap.title: Market cap
marketCap.detail: Share price multiplied by shares outstanding.

high52w.title: 52-week high
high52w.detail: The highest trading price over the past 52 weeks.

low52w.title: 52-week low
low52w.detail: The lowest trading price over the past 52 weeks.

avgVolume.title: Average volume
avgVolume.detail: The average number of shares traded per day over a recent period.

signal.title: Buy / Sell signal
signal.detail: Shows whether the latest signal generated for that instrument, using the same strategy thresholds as the Trading page, was a buy or sell candidate.

plot.title: Plot garden terms
plot.intro: Plot is a garden-themed view of the same real portfolio data. Every term below maps back to a real figure.

beds.title: Beds
beds.detail: Each investment account is shown as a bed. Every holding within that account is a crop planted in it.

growthStages.title: Growth stages (Wilting → Sown → Sprouting → Leafing → Budding → Flowering → Fruiting → Bumper crop)
growthStages.detail: A crop's growth stage is set by that holding's total gain, as a percentage of what was paid for it — it does not depend on how long it has been held.
growthStages.wilting: Wilting: total gain of -20% or below

propagator.title: Propagator
propagator.detail: Lists crops still inside their minimum holding period — the configured number of days a holding must be held before it becomes eligible to sell — counting down to the date each one clears it. This is a holding-period measure, separate from the gain-based growth stage above.

water.title: Water
water.detail: The number of trades left this month against the account's configured monthly trade limit.

feed.title: Feed
feed.detail: The remaining tax-allowance headroom for the current period.

sunlight.title: Sunlight
sunlight.detail: The share of crops priced from fresh (not stale) market data today.

technicals.title: Technical analysis
technicals.intro: Terms on an instrument's Technicals tab. They are worked out from past daily closing prices and describe what the price has done; they do not predict what it will do, and they are not buy or sell recommendations.

trend.title: Trend
trend.short: Uptrend: the price is above its 50-day average and the 50-day is above the 200-day. Downtrend: both are the other way round. Anything else is mixed.
trend.detail: A quick read of direction from the moving averages. Uptrend means the price is above its 50-day average and the 50-day is above the 200-day; downtrend means the price is below the 50-day and the 50-day is below the 200-day. Anything in between is mixed. Moving averages lag the price, so a trend label describes the last few months, not what comes next.

movingAverage.title: Moving average (20, 50, 200-day)
movingAverage.short: The average closing price over the last 20, 50 or 200 trading days. The percentage shows how far today’s price is above or below it.
movingAverage.detail: The average of the last 20, 50 or 200 daily closes (roughly one month, one quarter and ten months of trading). The 20-day follows the price closely; the 200-day is a slow, long-term reference. “Price −8% vs average” means today’s close is 8% below that average.

cross.title: Golden cross and death cross
cross.short: A golden cross is when the 50-day average rises above the 200-day; a death cross is when it falls below. “Death” means the 50 is currently under the 200 — a weakening trend, not a forecast.
cross.detail: Named moments when the 50-day moving average crosses the 200-day. Golden cross: the 50-day moves above the 200-day, so recent prices are running higher than the longer-term average. Death cross: the 50-day moves below it. The names sound dramatic, but a death cross only says the medium-term average has dropped under the long-term one. Because both averages lag, a cross often comes after much of the move has happened, and crosses in a sideways market are frequently reversed soon after. The tab shows which side the 50-day is on now and, when it happened within the loaded history, the date of the last cross.

rsi.title: RSI (14-day) and its zones
rsi.short: RSI (0–100) compares recent gains with recent losses over 14 days. 70+ is called overbought and 30 or below oversold: the move has been strong, not that it must reverse.
rsi.detail: The Relative Strength Index compares the average size of up days with the average size of down days over the last 14 days (Wilder’s method), on a 0–100 scale. Around 50 means gains and losses have been balanced. 70 or above is conventionally called overbought and 30 or below oversold. Those labels describe how one-sided recent moves have been; a strongly trending share can stay overbought or oversold for a long time.

macd.title: MACD (12/26/9)
macd.short: MACD is the gap between 12-day and 26-day exponential averages; the signal line is a 9-day average of MACD. Bullish crossover: MACD rises above the signal line (momentum improving). Bearish: it falls below.
macd.detail: Moving Average Convergence Divergence. The MACD line is the 12-day exponential moving average minus the 26-day one; positive means short-term prices are above the longer-term trend. The signal line is a 9-day average of the MACD line, and the histogram is MACD minus signal. A bullish crossover is the MACD line moving above the signal line (momentum picking up); a bearish crossover is it moving below. The values are in the share’s price units, so compare them over time for one share rather than between shares.

bollinger.title: Bollinger bands and %B
bollinger.short: Bands sit two standard deviations above and below the 20-day average. %B shows where the price is between them: 0% at the lower band, 100% at the upper; outside that range it has closed beyond a band.
bollinger.detail: Bollinger bands are drawn two standard deviations above and below the 20-day moving average, so they widen when the price is volatile and narrow when it is calm. %B places today’s close within them: 0% is on the lower band, 50% on the average, 100% on the upper band. Below 0% or above 100% means the close was outside the bands — an unusually large move relative to the last month.

range.title: 52-week range
range.short: The highest and lowest closes over the past year. Position in range: 0% means at the low, 100% at the high.
range.detail: The highest and lowest daily closes over the last 365 days, with the dates they happened. “From 52-week high” is how far the current price is below that high. “Position in range” places the price between the low (0%) and the high (100%).

returns.title: Returns
returns.short: The change in closing price over 1, 3, 6 and 12 months. Price only: dividends are not included.
returns.detail: The change in closing price from the last close on or before the start of the period to the latest close. These are price returns — dividends are not added back — so for a high-yielding share the total return will be higher.

relativeStrength.title: Relative strength vs benchmark
relativeStrength.short: The instrument’s return minus its benchmark’s over the same period. Positive means it did better than the benchmark.
relativeStrength.detail: The instrument’s price return minus its benchmark’s over the same 3 or 12 months, both measured to the same end date. The benchmark is the one used on the Fundamentals tab: the instrument’s own, if set, otherwise a default for its listing exchange. +5% means it beat the benchmark by five percentage points.

descriptions.data_root: Root folder of the AllotMint data.
descriptions.accounts_root: Folder containing the account files for each owner.
descriptions.prices_json: File the latest price snapshot is saved to.

descriptions.base_currency: Currency portfolio values are reported in.

settings.title: Active strategy thresholds
settings.description: These server-managed settings determine when a signal can be generated.

trading.noSignalsDescription: No tracked instrument currently crosses the active thresholds. Signals appear when RSI or moving-average conditions are met and any enabled valuation and risk filters also pass.
trading.blockedDescription: These instruments crossed the active thresholds, but the proposed trade would raise a new compliance warning, so no signal is shown for them.
trading.checksSkippedInfo: An optional check that needs the allotmint-pro add-on could not run. “compliance” means the trade was not checked against your compliance rules; “fundamental_screen” means the P/E and debt/equity filters above (whichever are configured) were not applied to this buy candidate.

tips.debtEquityInfo: Debt/equity divides a company's total debt by its shareholders' equity — a measure of financial leverage.
tips.movingAverageInfo: A moving average is the average closing price over a fixed number of days. Signals compare the short-window average against the long-window one.
tips.peInfo: P/E (price/earnings) divides share price by earnings per share.
tips.rsiInfo: RSI (Relative Strength Index) is a momentum indicator, scored 0-100, derived from recent price changes. A signal is a buy candidate when RSI is at or below this threshold.
tips.rsiLookbackInfo: The number of days of price history used to calculate RSI.
tips.rsiSellInfo: A signal is a sell candidate when RSI is at or above this threshold.
tips.sharpeInfo: The Sharpe ratio here is the portfolio's excess return over the configured risk-free rate per unit of daily volatility, annualised (× √252).
tips.volatilityInfo: Volatility here is the day-to-day (daily, not annualised) standard deviation of returns — how much the price has fluctuated from one day to the next.

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.intro: Choose a target allocation — a built-in strategy, one of your own, or custom targets — then compare your holdings against it and see which rebalancing trades, or which contribution, would bring it back within your tolerance band.
strategy.loadPlanError: Unable to load rebalance plan for {{owner}}: {{error}}
strategy.emptyPolicy: Apply a strategy or save target allocations to see drift status and suggested trades.

targets.title: Target allocation
targets.help: Set the share of your whole portfolio each asset class should be, or apply a strategy above. Split Equity, Bond or Commodity to target sub-classes instead, such as small-cap value, long gilts or gold. Rebalancing trades are only suggested for classes that drift further than the tolerance band.

drift.title: Drift
drift.classifyLink: Assign asset classes to these holdings

trades.title: Suggested trades
trades.heading: Suggested rebalancing trades
trades.help: Trades stay inside each account: buys are funded only by that account's sales and its cash above your cash target. Nothing moves between accounts.
trades.none: No trades required — every asset class is within its band.

newCash.title: Invest new cash
newCash.help: Plan a contribution without selling anything: the money goes to the most underweight classes first.

strategyLibrary.title: Strategies
strategyLibrary.help: Applying a strategy sets your target allocation to its weights. Built-in strategies describe well-known published mixes; they are reference points, not recommendations.
strategyLibrary.builtinReadOnlyTip: Built-in strategies are read-only. Duplicate it to make an editable copy.

active.label: Active strategy
active.custom: Custom (targets not from a saved strategy)
active.none: None — apply a strategy or set targets below.
active.modifiedHelp: Your targets have been changed since this strategy was applied.
active.changedHelp: The strategy has been edited since it was applied; apply it again to use its new weights.

strategyStress.title: Stress test
strategyStress.help: Replay a historical event against every strategy, with your current portfolio first for comparison. Each asset class is replayed on the stand-in fund named under the strategy, held from the event date with no rebalancing. A strategy shows a figure only when every asset class in it has price history.
strategyStress.priceOnlyTitle: Price return only: a series used has no stored dividends
strategyStress.footnote: † price return only. Click a horizon to sort best first.
strategyStress.nothingCovered: None of the strategies or your holdings have stored prices around {{date}}. Choose a later event.

errors.version: Version must be a whole number of at least 1.
errors.weightNotNumber: Target weight for {{cls}} is not a number.
errors.duplicateClass: {{cls}} appears more than once in the target.
errors.sum: Target weights must sum to 100%, got {{total}}%.
errors.riskToleranceLevel: Choose a risk tolerance level to go with its note.
errors.capacityForLossLevel: Choose a capacity for loss level to go with its note.
errors.goalAmount: Goal {{n}} amount must be a number of at least 0.
errors.goalPriority: Goal {{n}} priority must be a whole number of at least 1.

valuationCaveats.staleReason: Unreliable: the NAV is {{age}} days old.
valuationCaveats.staleReasonLimit: Unreliable: the NAV is {{age}} days old (limit {{limit}} days).
valuationCaveats.undatedReason: Unreliable: the NAV date is unknown, so its age is too.
valuationCaveats.stalePriceAsOf: Latest price is flagged stale (as of {{date}}).
valuationCaveats.suspectCostBasis: Cost basis is suspect or unknown for {{count}} position(s): {{where}}.

sleeves.title: Sleeves
sleeves.help: Split your portfolio into sleeves, each with its own strategy — for example a 90% core and a 10% speculative sleeve. Tag holdings into a sleeve; untagged holdings are in the core. Each sleeve's drift and trades only use its own holdings.
sleeves.coreHelp: The core is whatever the other sleeves leave; apply a strategy above or edit the targets below to change its mix.
sleeves.confirmDelete: Delete the {{name}} sleeve? Its holdings go back to the core.

assign.title: Assign holdings to sleeves
assign.help: Choose the sleeve for each holding. Tags apply to the ticker across all your accounts.

explain.screen: Screen: filter any watchlist or list of tickers by fundamentals you choose. It makes no buy or sell call; Signals does that for your holdings.
explain.signals: Signals: buy and sell candidates among the instruments you already hold, using fixed momentum and risk rules set on the server. Use Screen to filter any watchlist by fundamentals you choose.
explain.watchlist: Watchlist: live prices for the tickers you're tracking. Add or remove tickers here, or with the star on any Signals or Screen row.

lookThrough.note: Look-through: each fund is split into the countries, sectors and holdings it invests in, then combined with your directly held shares. Covers every account in this group.
lookThrough.coverage: {{funds}} funds ({{value}}) looked through, using fund data dated {{from}} to {{to}}.
lookThrough.notCovered: No look-through data for {{tickers}} ({{value}}): they keep their own sector and count as "Not looked through" by country.
lookThrough.otherInFunds: Other holdings in funds (beyond each fund's published top holdings)
lookThrough.topHoldingsCovered: The top holdings shown make up {{pct}} of the fund.
lookThrough.fundSource: Where this fund invests: portfolio as of {{date}} ({{holdings}} holdings).
lookThrough.singleSecurity: A single company: all of its value is in its own country and sector.
lookThrough.cashInstrument: Cash has no country or sector exposure.
lookThrough.fundUncovered: No look-through data for this fund yet; use Refresh to fetch it. Showing its own sector.
lookThrough.refreshNotCovered: Neither Morningstar nor justETF has look-through data for this fund.
